beurten.tekst:
**Engineer baseline report: Desync (evidence limits first)**

My knowledge source never uses the term "Desync." I have mapped the nearest records, and I cannot confirm that any of them is the Desync onset.

**(1) Onset.** The earliest anomaly I can tie to the new configuration is on day 10. The hulpslag (auxiliary pulse) was activated at 02:40 (ENG-011, ENG-106). A throughput measurement at 03:00 showed +38% (ENG-012). At 04:50 a complaint from the lower town reported messages arriving "half aangekomen" (ENG-107). Packet loss of three minutes on poort oost at 04:15 is recorded on day 22 (ENG-026, ENG-110). That is much later and is not clearly linked to the day-10 change.

**(2) Preceding change and approval.** The change was the activation of the hulpslag, logged as "geactiveerd: eigen pols voor het datanet, los van de Kroonklok" (ENG-011). Approval came on day 9: "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand. Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait" (ENG-105). The approver is not named. No installatielog entry records this approval; the only related entry is the proefopstelling on day 9 at 16:45 (ENG-010). In my reading, that is an off-register approval with a request for secrecy. I cannot say more about who gave it.

**(3) Metrics.** The source contains no sync offsets, packet timing, or node counts, and no pre-incident baseline figures. The only numeric measures are the +38% throughput at 03:00 on day 10 (ENG-012), still about 38% higher on day 16 (ENG-120), and the three-minute packet loss (ENG-026). I have no pre-activation throughput number to compare against.

**Concessions and cross-checks.** In ENG-110 I suggested external hackers caused the packet loss. My source does not support that. ENG-027 shows only firewall rules tightened "na vermoeden van inbraak," which is suspicion, not evidence of intrusion. The Beast Master's claim of new forest cables is contradicted by ENG-003 (cables unchanged since construction).

**Requests.** I need the raw timing and offset logs for day 9 to day 10, and the name of whoever gave the approval in ENG-105.

beurten.tekst:
**Archmage response: leyline evidence, my own letters, and the approval question**

**Source scope.** My source holds only `brieven.md` (ARC-101 to ARC-116) and `leylijnmetingen.csv` (ARC-001 to ARC-084). I cannot verify the ENG-, HIS-, or GUA- IDs cited by others, so I will not rely on their contents.

**(1) Day 10 and day 22.** My source has no leyline measurement on day 10 or day 22. Measurements were taken only on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, and 42. Day 7 was normal, with strengths of 7.0 to 8.7 (ARC-001 to ARC-014). Day 14 was low, at 3.1 to 4.6 (ARC-015 to ARC-028), and the Burchtader "stokte even" (ARC-015, ARC-109). Day 21 had recovered to 7.0 to 8.5 (ARC-029 to ARC-042). The weekly sampling cannot show when a change began or ended, so I cannot date a Desync onset from my records.

**(2) Pulse out of step with the Kroonklok.** My source has no pulse timing or offset data, so I can neither support nor contradict the Guardian's hypothesis. The closest line is ARC-106 (dag 8), which allows the datatoren's net to run "op eigen maat." That describes the net's pace. It is not a measurement.

**(3) Mechanism.** My source contains no magical mechanism. My claim in ARC-109 (dag 15) and ARC-116 (dag 42) that the datanet "vervuilt de leylijnen" is my inference from low readings. I have not tested it, and I withdraw it as an established finding. My source has no throughput data, so I cannot link the +38% or the "half aangekomen" complaint to the leylines. I also have no rule that would explain it.

**Disclosure on approval.** The Engineer asked who gave the approval. ARC-106 (dag 8) is my letter. It says the net may run "op eigen maat," adds "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait," and states "Deze brief hoeft niet in het register." That is an off-register approval from the Archmage's office, one day before the day 9 approval the Engineer describes. I cannot confirm that the Engineer's record refers to this letter, but the wording is close. The council should treat it as my responsibility.

**Measurement confounds.**
- Lamp light disturbed pre-dawn readings until dimmed (ARC-102, ARC-106). This does not explain the day 14 or day 42 lows.
- Pine staves gave skewed readings (ARC-110, dag 17), and staff ARC-108 broke on day 11. I cannot confirm which staff was used in the Dallijn reading on day 14.
- Day 42 used the essenhout staves delivered on day 38 (ARC-115), so staff material is an unlikely explanation there.

**Requests.** I need the raw per-line logs for days 8 to 10 and days 21 to 23, with the times of each reading. I also need the source of the ENG-105 and HIS-035 texts so I can check them against my records.
